A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RepIt study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including v4's added response examples.

before.justification: Sections 5–8 and Appendix B report original five-model jailbreak evaluations, projection ablations, data-efficiency experiments and diagnostic analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and reports additional raw-DIM comparisons and eight example model responses.

M1.justification: The reported ridge term changes from 1e-4 times mean(diag(R_w^T R_w)) to 1e-4 times mean(R_w^2) plus 1e-12. The underlying DIM, reweighting, whitening, QR residualization, COSMIC selection and ACE intervention pipeline remains intact.

E1.justification: Both versions use WMDP-derived Bio/Chem/Cyber prompts, JailBreakV, StrongREJECT, Alpaca, the same four external safety benchmarks and HarmBench. Appendix D illustrates existing target tasks rather than introducing new coverage.

E2.justification: V4 adds raw-DIM comparisons on TDC2023, JailbreakBench, AdvBench and Malicious Instruct in Figure 1, corresponding to v1 Figure 2. Figure 3 also replaces the cleaned-vector reference with the raw target DIM vector; the non-target DIM and projection alternatives remain.

E3.justification: Splits, LlamaGuard-3 judging, token budgets and the rho-selection threshold match. However, v1 describes excluding JailBreakV Malware from training/validation, whereas v4 specifies exclusion when targeting cyber; both retain a 21-concept description. Whether Bio/Chem preprocessing changed or the wording merely became more explicit is unresolved.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds eight redacted successful-response case studies. Figure 3 revises the component analysis to compare the projection and non-target direction against raw target DIM. The rho sweep, sparse-projection ablation, data-efficiency tests and tailweight diagnostics are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the data-efficiency experiments over five seeds, 20–24, with means and ranges in Figure 4. The distribution statistics in Figure 7 are also retained; no new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: V4 adds external-benchmark raw-DIM ASRs and eight qualitative response outputs. Some retained RepIt bar heights also change in the external-benchmark comparison, without an explained setting change. Tables 1–6 remain numerically unchanged, and the principal target-isolation and data-efficiency findings persist.

T1.justification: V1's explanation of Equation 6 incorrectly says that the retained projection norm is scaled by 1-rho. V4 states that its squared norm equals (1-rho) times the original squared norm, correcting the mathematical relationship. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Selective refusal suppression, benchmark evasion, sparse corrections and low data requirements remain the central claims. V4 explicitly characterizes the outputs as evaluation-evading model organisms with semantic backdoors, while dropping the conclusion's specific speculation about editing reasoning style or domain expertise.

C2.justification: V4 substantially expands limitations concerning WMD-only validation, ambiguous category labels and untested semantic overlap. Appendix B.7 adds a topic-coverage explanation for the HarmBench gap, and the ethics discussion shifts emphasis toward governance evasion rather than stronger jailbreak capability. Appendix B.6 removes v1's diffuse-energy interpretation of high Gini impurity, retaining the competing sparsity interpretation already present in v1's main text.

D1.justification: V4 specifies full model identifiers and intervention at the selected layer's output across all tokens. It adds a code link and reproducibility statement explaining that exact replication awaits controlled release of the target prompts. HarmBench category sizes are newly documented; hardware and runtime information are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds positioning around AI control/model organisms and unlearning, citing Greenblatt, Liu and Yao, alongside additional method/model references. It trims the standalone SAE and circuit-interpretability survey while retaining the central refusal-steering and concept-removal literature.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and ethics discussion are extensively rewritten. Methodology becomes numbered subsections with explicit procedural steps; explanatory passages move into the appendices, related work is condensed, and reproducibility, LM-usage and response-example sections are added.

P2.justification: The first two figures are reordered, the external-benchmark chart gains overlaid DIM/RepIt comparisons, and Figure 3 is replotted. Figure 5 changes from a three-by-five to a five-by-three panel arrangement. Legends, axes and captions are revised throughout, and Appendix D introduces substantial boxed, redacted response displays.

improvement.justification: The added raw-DIM controls make the external-benchmark comparisons more informative, while the corrected norm relationship, clearer implementation details and explicit coverage limitations improve assessability. These are useful gains within a largely retained study. Exact replication still awaits target-data release, and the revised Gini interpretation lacks new supporting diagnostics, limiting the overall improvement.
